verdict.rationale: Conductor's docs show it creates a dedicated branch for each workspace and helps open a pull request when the work is ready. Nothing documents the agent staging changes or writing commit messages, and the PR step is framed as Conductor helping the user rather than the agent doing it on its own. Missing for 10: documented agent-driven staging, commit-message generation, explicit agent-initiated PR creation, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the git workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent stage changes, write commit messages, create branches, and open pull requests

citations.quote: When the work is ready, Conductor helps you review the diff, open a pull request, merge, and archive the workspace.
Each task gets its own workspace, branch, files, terminal, diff, and review path.
Create a new workspace with Command + N when work should have its own branch, files, running environment, and review path.
